subject: [RFC PATCH 3/4] memcg_ext: allow BPF to defer memory.high enforcement

2026-09-21.patch_summary: This patch allows BPF (Berkeley Packet Filter) programs to defer memory.high enforcement, which prevents tasks holding kernel locks from being stuck in the charge path. It introduces high_policy ops that provide a read-only snapshot of the charge and allow programs to return a request. This approach enables more efficient handling of memory allocation and deallocation by allowing BPF programs to manage memory usage without blocking other tasks.

reviews.author: JP Kobryn
reviews.summary: Reviewer JP Kobryn noted that the gfp_mask passed to BPF programs does not account for task restrictions, which could lead to unexpected behavior if __GFP_FS or __GFP_IO flags are later cleared when setting up scan_control.
reviews.raw_body:
If I'm reading correctly, the gfp_mask at this point doesn't account for
task restrictions, so the BPF program may see __GFP_FS, __GFP_IO, etc
which may later be cleared when setting up the scan_control instance.

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged that the swapoff path needs to drop the per-vswap spinlock before calling try_to_unmap(), agreed to restructure in v2.

The author is addressing a concern about passing the correct GFP flags to __mem_cgroup_handle_over_high(). They explain that they are passing the same gfp_mask as try_charge_memcg(), which should be consistent with what reclaim_high sees.
reviews.raw_body:
On Thu, Sep 24, 2026 at 01:14:59PM -0700, JP Kobryn wrote:
[...]

---

I am passing the same gfp_mask which has been passed to try_charge_memcg(), so
it should be same as what reclaim_high (reclaim internal) sees.
